meta.title: The Prism of Perception: Cognitive Bias Analysis
meta.description: Explore the labyrinth of human cognition and reveal the subtle distortions that shape your reality.
meta.keywords: cognitive structure, mental heuristics, psychology of perception, wisdom diagnosis

confirmation_bias.name: Confirmation Bias
confirmation_bias.subtitle: The Echo Chamber of the Self
confirmation_bias.description: A subconscious tendency to seek, interpret, and favor information that aligns with one's established sanctuary of belief, while excluding dissonant truths.
examples: Selectively justifying data that mirrors your existing worldview.
Confining yourself within the circle of one-sided relationships that only echo your own voice.
overcome: Intentionally inhabit the perspective of the 'Other.'
Meditate on the following question: 'What truth could render my current conviction false?'

authority_bias.name: Authority Bias
authority_bias.subtitle: Adoration of the Crown
authority_bias.description: The tendency to grant excessive weight and accuracy to the declarations of perceived authorities, silencing one's own critical insights.
examples: Accepting a specific doctrine simply because it was uttered by a renowned 'sage.'
Hesitating to question obvious errors originating from those draped in the robes of power.
overcome: Look closely at the reality of the message itself, detached from the status of the messenger.
Remember that even those atop the highest altars are not immune to human imperfection.

availability_heuristic.name: Availability Heuristic
availability_heuristic.subtitle: Tyranny of Immediacy
availability_heuristic.description: The error of judging the probability of events based solely on examples that easily come to mind, often swayed by recent emotions rather than statistical reality.
examples: Fearing rare, lightning-like shocks more than the quiet, persistent systemic risks that remain invisible.
Gauging the state of the world through the prism of sensationalist headlines.
overcome: Face the cold and absolute geometry of statistics.
Do not allow a single intense story to overshadow the universal truth of countless existences.

anchoring_bias.name: Anchoring Bias
anchoring_bias.subtitle: Gravity of First Impressions
anchoring_bias.description: The tendency to remain tethered to the first fragment of information encountered, subordinating all subsequent revelations to that initial anchor.
examples: Accepting a price as just simply because a more absurd price preceded it.
Allowing initial estimates to cast a shadow over all future calculations.
overcome: Discard the first numbers presented as mere illusions of context.
Before the world drops its anchor upon you, establish your own independent baseline.

dunning_kruger.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
dunning_kruger.subtitle: Illusion of Early Mastery
dunning_kruger.description: A state of cognitive dissonance where those with shallow depth in a field possess the greatest confidence, failing to recognize the vast ocean of complexity they have yet to navigate.
examples: Mistaking the acquisition of basic terminology for the mastery of a discipline.
Dismissing a specific task as trivial before ever handling the mechanisms of its execution.
overcome: Maintain a 'Beginner's Mind' even as you make progress.
Seek the critique of masters to map the true boundaries of your understanding.

survivorship_bias.name: Survivorship Bias
survivorship_bias.subtitle: Silence of the Departed
survivorship_bias.description: A logical fallacy of focusing only on those who successfully passed through a selection process, while overlooking the countless failures resting in invisible graves.
examples: Studying only the footprints of giants while forgetting the many who vanished on the same path.
Attributing a result solely to willpower, though it was merely the outcome of fluctuations among the masses.
overcome: Seek the stories of those who did not succeed to understand the true cost of the path.
Ask: 'What data is missing from this narrative of victory?'
